issues.description: The problem statement and tests require public getters for all attributes of ExcellenceLand (a boolean attribute 'excellentEnough'), implying a no-argument getter (e.g., isExcellentEnough()). However, the solution implements isExcellentEnough(boolean strictCheck) which takes a boolean parameter. This signature mismatch will confuse students about the expected getter signature and will not satisfy the test/check that expects a parameterless getter.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the getter in ExcellenceLand to a parameterless method that returns the boolean attribute, e.g. public boolean isExcellentEnough() { return excellentEnough; }. Ensure the constructor and other getters remain unchanged so they match the UML and test expectations.

issues.description: The UML / problem statement defines the boolean attribute 'excellentEnough' in ExcellenceLand and requires a public getter for it. The solution declares a method isExcellentEnough(boolean strictCheck) (same identifier but with a boolean parameter) instead of a no-argument getter. This signature mismatch (getter expected with no parameters vs. solution method taking a parameter) breaks the direct mapping between the problem requirement (add public getters) and the implemented API and will confuse students looking for the standard getter for 'excellentEnough'.
issues.suggestedFix: Provide a standard no-argument getter for the boolean attribute, e.g. public boolean isExcellentEnough() { return excellentEnough; }, or if a parameterized check is required, rename the existing method to something like checkExcellentEnough(boolean strictCheck) and also add the standard getter isExcellentEnough() so the UML requirement (public getter) is satisfied and student mapping is clear.
